discovery: Quantum key distribution: cryptographic security founded on the laws of quantum physics

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Research, Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the no-cloning property and measurement disturbance of single quantum systems allow two parties to establish a secret key whose security rests on physical law rather than computational assumptions. Ekert (E91) independently linked key secrecy to the violation of Bell inequalities, turning a foundational test of nonlocality into a cryptographic resource and seeding today's device-independent security and certified randomness. These ideas opened the field of quantum information and have been experimentally realised across ever harsher channels: metropolitan fibre networks, daylight free-space links, and satellite-to-ground links spanning more than a thousand kilometres. Quantum key distribution is now entering standards and real communication infrastructure worldwide. Few conceptual discoveries in physics have so directly produced a new technological capability while also deepening our understanding of entanglement and measurement.
